title: RGCL Origin / Source-to-Coframe Variational Pairing Gate
scope: current frozen ontology and the four named candidate pairing classes only

theorem.name: Scale-Weight Pairing Obstruction
theorem.statement: Within the audited frozen candidate class, weight-zero geometry objects paired with nonzero weight-one source objects remain weight one. Making the result invariant under the exact positive source reparameterization removes amplitude and leaves only projective information. A nonzero source-extensive, parameterization-independent absolute coupling therefore requires an independently calibrated negative-weight object or equivalent new law.
theorem.not_claimed: This is not a theorem that no deeper nonlinear ontology can generate a coupling.

candidate_reasons.genesis_measure_support: Retained grade and measure/support can localize or weight source amount but do not supply a unique coframe/tensor embedding or a calibrated retained-to-geometry conversion factor.
candidate_reasons.pgrl_bkm: At fixed state BKM is source-scale weight zero while tangent duals/norms inherit source amplitude; normalization removes amplitude and leaves only projective data.
candidate_reasons.resa_solder_coframe: A supplied solder can conditionally provide a type map but does not fix magnitude, and v13.11 already proves the same quantum response admits nonunique solder/coframe lifts.
candidate_reasons.qmar_response_covariance: QMAR is covariant but source-linear; covariance and exact trace identities constrain form, not the absolute coefficient, and visible geometry is not an autonomous source state.

positive_control.construction: Supply an explicit inverse-weight calibration g(a)=g0/a.
positive_control.result: The weight-one candidate becomes invariant to machine precision.
positive_control.interpretation: A compensating calibration is sufficient, but it is not present in the frozen ontology and therefore would be added structure.
